approvalScope: One ordinary private Node.js 20 Actor candidate and a three-row smoke run; only if the smoke gate passes, use the same build for the full 100-row acceptance run under the TID route.
flow: Actor.getInput -> bounded ordinary publisher HTTP fetch -> structured articleBody then Mozilla Readability on the same in-memory response -> Actor.pushData to the default dataset.

acceptance.deduplication: Disabled; all 100 original row occurrences remain separate.

scoring.fullTextTarget: At least 50 independently reviewed readable article texts across all 100 rows.
scoring.candidateRule: Nonempty extracted text, word count and extractor status are evidence inputs only; they do not alone prove readable article text.
scoring.qualityReview: Exclude navigation, login, cookie, challenge, subscription and error-page text. Do not add an arbitrary minimum word-count threshold.

costModel.full900SecondComputeEstimate: About 0.0625 compute units / $0.0125 at the previously referenced $0.20 per compute-unit standard rate.
costModel.uncertainty: Actual account rates, bandwidth, build, storage and API costs may differ; record actual hosted usage and cost.

stopRules: Do not continue from smoke to acceptance unless smoke produces a row output for each input and demonstrates eligible fetched HTML reaching extraction and normal dataset output.
Do not repeat an unchanged failed candidate.
If fewer than 50 rows yield eligible HTML in acceptance, report the access-limited result and stop; do not run B3.
Run B3 only if at least 50 eligible HTML responses are fetched and independent quality review shows extraction quality is the remaining blocker.
Retain metrics and hashes in Git; retain no full HTML or article text in Git.
